title: The if Statement
objective: Run code conditionally with if and if-else.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material. List-dependent if-statement patterns are covered later in the Collections chapter, after lists are introduced.

paragraphs: An if statement runs a block of code only when its condition is True. Write if, then a Boolean expression, then a colon; the indented lines below run only when that expression is True.

Indentation is not just style in Python — it's how the language knows which lines belong to the if block. Every line indented the same amount right after the if line is part of that block; the first line back at the original indentation ends it.

Adding else gives you a second block that runs only when the condition is False. Together, if and else cover both possible outcomes of a single condition — exactly one of the two blocks runs, never both, never neither.
explanation.rule: The indented lines under if run only when the condition is True; the indented lines under else run only when it's False.

examples.title: One Path or the Other
examples.note: Since 900 is less than 1200, only the else block runs.

checks.question: In an if/else statement, how many of the two blocks run for a single check?
options: Exactly one, whichever matches the condition.

feedback.correct: Correct — if/else is an either/or; exactly one branch executes.
feedback.incorrect: if/else always picks exactly one branch based on the condition's value.

assignment.title: Heat Check
assignment.brief: Write heat_check(temperature) that prints 'Ready to forge.' if temperature is at least 1200, otherwise prints 'Keep heating.'
requirements: Print the correct message for each case.
assignment.starterCode:
def heat_check(temperature):
    # Use if/else to print the right message.
    pass

heat_check(900)
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    heat_check(900)
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: The if block runs when the condition is True; the else block runs when it's False.
Indent both print() calls the same amount, one level in from if/else.
900 is less than 1200, so the else branch should run for this call.
